data.gender_notes: Philippa is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Follower of Horses, Derived from the Greek name Philippos. The name Philippa carries the meaning “Lover of horses” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Philippa usually hope their child will grow to embody lover of horses and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes strength, courage, and determination. Represents the connection between the earth and the divine.
data.etymology: Philippa belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lover of horses.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Philippa total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_latin.name: Philippa
in_latin.long_meaning: nomen femininum originis Graecae, significatio 'amabilis patrum' (patres Ecclesiae), uti in Novo Testamento, frequens in Ecclesia Christiana, et dignum significatio culturalem et religiosam in traditione Christiana.

in_english.name: Philippa
in_english.long_meaning: a feminine given name of Greek origin, meaning 'loved by the fathers' (fathers of the Church), as in the New Testament, commonly found in Christian cultures, with significant cultural and religious importance in Christian tradition, associated with the virtues of devotion, loyalty, and compassion, often bestowed upon girls born to families of Christian faith.

data.cultural_impact: The name Philippa, derived from the Greek name Philippos, has a rich history and cultural significance. The name Philippa was quite popular in the Middle Ages, particularly among the nobility and ruling classes in Europe. It is also the name of several prominent figures throughout history, such as St. Philip the Deacon, a disciple of Jesus Christ, and Queen Philippa of England, who ruled during the late 13th and early 14th centuries.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Philippa holds spiritual significance as it comes from the Greek name Philippos, which means "horse-loving" or "horse-friendly." In Christian tradition, the name Philippa can be seen as a reminder of the symbolism of the horse in biblical literature. Horses are often depicted as powerful and majestic creatures, representing strength, endurance, and mobility, qualities that are sought after in those who follow God.
